transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s starting to scare me. My brain just feels completely foggy, and I find myself freezing up even when I'm trying to do the simplest tasks.
Besides this brain fog and difficulty making decisions, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or unusually anxious for most of the day over the past few weeks?

Yes, I really have. Most days when I walk into the clinic or sit down to study, I feel like there's this heavy, gray cloud sitting on my chest. Even when nothing bad is happening, I just feel sad and hopeless for no clear reason and I can't shake it.
Did these feelings of sadness and difficulty concentrating begin specifically after a recent stressful life event or significant change in your life?

Yes, they started about a year ago when I began juggling full-time shifts at the clinic while starting my first college nursing classes. A severe staffing shortage turned my orientation into weeks of exhausting, back-to-back shifts, which completely overwhelmed my routines. That intense stress is what really triggered this whole downward spiral.

Since those initial stressful events a year ago, have you felt that your symptoms are primarily a reaction to the ongoing pressures of your work and school, or do you feel these feelings have persisted even when you have managed to take a break or get time away from those stressors?

These feelings definitely persist even when I have a break from work or school. On my days off, I still feel completely sad, hopeless, and exhausted, and I usually just lie in bed unable to enjoy anything. It has become a constant state that I can't seem to shake, no matter what.
Have you noticed other physical changes during this time, such as significant shifts in your appetite, your sleep patterns, or a total loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed?

Yes, I've noticed all of those. My appetite is completely gone and my scrubs are starting to hang off me because food just makes me feel nauseous. I also struggle to sleep because my mind races until 3 a.m., and I've lost all interest in jogging or knitting, choosing to just lie in bed scrolling on my phone and ignoring my friends.

Do you feel like your movements and speech have become noticeably slowed down to the point where others might have commented on it, or do you feel a sense of intense, restless agitation that makes it hard to sit still?

My coworkers have actually commented that I move like I'm in slow motion now. Doing basic tasks like walking down the hall or pulling meds feels like wading through molasses, and I don't feel restless or agitated at all. Sometimes I just find myself staring at the computer screen for minutes before I can even make my hands start charting.

Given how significant these symptoms are, do you find yourself completely unable to function in your daily activities, or are you still managing to perform the essential tasks of your work and studies, even if it is with extreme difficulty?

I'm still trying to push through and manage, but it is with extreme difficulty and I'm falling behind on everything. I've already gotten written up at the clinic for charting errors, my grades are slipping, and I've completely stopped seeing my friends. It really feels like both my career plans and my social life are falling apart.

latest_inference.note: The patient describes a persistent state of sadness, loss of interest (anhedonia), significant physical symptoms (weight loss, sleep disturbance), and psychomotor retardation that have persisted for a year. The symptoms are severe enough to cause significant functional impairment at work and school, even in the absence of external stressors. The presence of marked psychomotor retardation and the severity of the functional impairment support the inclusion of F32.2 (severe without psychotic symptoms), while the ongoing struggle to function maintains the possibility of F32.1 (moderate).
